source: Written for this site. Each entry says what a box means, where to find the number, and what to do if unsure.
confidenceNote: Words, not figures. Where an entry names a figure it is the one in the data file beside it.

name.q: What should the site call your household?
name.what: A label at the top of every page, nothing more. Leave it blank and it says Your household.

region.what: The typical tuition bands differ most by region: the New York and New Jersey metro is highest, the other large communities next, smaller communities lowest. A price you type on the tuition page replaces the band.
region.where: Where the school is, not where you work.
region.unsure: Pick the closest. Then type the school's own numbers on the tuition page and the region stops mattering.

community.q: Which community is the house in?
community.what: Sets a typical home price and property tax rate for the home page. A price you type there replaces it.
community.unsure: Choose Not listed; the home page then asks for the price.

gross.q: What do both earners make in a year, before anything is taken out?
gross.what: Salary, bonus, self-employment profit, added up, before tax. Tzedakah on the gross base and the life cover check read it.
gross.where: The last pay stub's year-to-date gross, scaled to twelve months, or line 1 of last year's return plus what has changed.
gross.unsure: Type the salary you know and come back for the rest.

takeHome.q: What lands in the bank in an ordinary month, after tax and retirement?
takeHome.what: The sum of every paycheck and profit draw in a month, after tax, health premiums and retirement have come out. The picture page starts from it.
takeHome.where: The net line on each pay stub, added up over a month; a bank statement's deposits if pay is irregular.
takeHome.unsure: Add up last month's deposits from work.

retirement.q: How much goes to retirement each month, from both of you?
retirement.what: Your own contributions to a 401(k), 403(b), IRA or the like. The employer match is not yours to count here.
retirement.where: The pay stub's 401(k) line, times the paychecks in a month.
retirement.unsure: Type what one of you puts in; add the other later.

parentBirthYear.q: What year was the older parent born?
parentBirthYear.what: The picture page works out how many years run from the last tuition bill to that parent's 65th birthday, and what the freed tuition could grow to in them.
parentBirthYear.unsure: Leave it blank; the picture page says what it needs.

birthYear.q: What year was this child born?
birthYear.what: Places the child in a grade each school year, an age for camp, and a year for each simcha. Kindergarten starts in the September of the year they turn five.
birthYear.unsure: A year is enough; the month does not matter here.

sex.what: A bar mitzvah lands at thirteen, a bat mitzvah at twelve. Nothing else on the site reads it.
sex.unsure: Leave it; the child has no bar or bat mitzvah on the line until it is set.

gapYear.q: Will this child spend the year after high school in Israel?
gapYear.what: Yes adds a year of tuition at eighteen on the tuition page and a stop on the simchas line. It is the norm in most Modern Orthodox high schools, and most families do not know at five.
gapYear.unsure: Leave it as Not sure; the years are drawn without it. Come back when the child is fourteen.

camp.q: Where does this child spend the summer?
camp.what: Sleepaway camp is usually ages nine to sixteen, day camp three to ten. The year page prices whichever you choose, at the price you type there.
camp.unsure: Choose No camp for a child under three, and the camp the older siblings went to for the rest.

assistanceShare.q: What reduction did the tuition committee give?
assistanceShare.what: The share taken off full tuition, applied to every child. A family paying 21,000 on a 28,000 tuition has a 25% reduction.
assistanceShare.where: The award letter, or the bill against the published schedule.
assistanceShare.unsure: Leave it blank if you pay in full. If you have applied and are waiting, leave it blank and see the full figure.

siblingShare.q: Does the school discount the third child onward?
siblingShare.what: Some schools take a few percent off from the third or fourth child in the school at once. Many give none.

siblingFrom.q: From which child does the discount start?
siblingFrom.what: Counted by the children in school in the same year, oldest first. Three means the third child in school and every one after.

stage_early.q: What does the school charge for nursery or pre-K, a year, before assistance?
stage_early.what: The two years before kindergarten, at ages three and four. Often a separate schedule from the main school, and often eligible for the dependent care account.
stage_early.unsure: Leave it blank and the region's typical figure is used, marked assumed.

stage_elementary.q: What does the school charge for kindergarten to eighth grade, a year, before assistance?
stage_elementary.what: The full published figure, before the committee's reduction. Fees, the building fund and busing are not in it; the year page has room for them if you want them counted.
stage_elementary.where: The tuition schedule on the school's site or in the enrolment packet.
stage_elementary.unsure: Leave it blank and the region's typical figure is used, marked assumed.

stage_high.q: What does the high school charge, a year, before assistance?
stage_high.what: Ninth to twelfth grade. Often a different school from the elementary, with its own committee.
stage_high.unsure: Leave it blank and the region's typical figure is used, marked assumed.

stage_gap.q: What will the year in Israel cost, after grants?
stage_gap.what: Tuition, room and board, and two flights, less the MASA grant and the program's own aid. Assistance and sibling discounts do not apply to it.
stage_gap.where: The yeshiva or seminary's published fee, and the MASA site for the grant.
stage_gap.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical figure is used, marked assumed.

event_shul.q: What are the shul's dues for the family, a year?
event_shul.what: Full membership. Many shuls bill in Elul. Relief is common and quiet; ask if it is heavy.
event_shul.where: The dues letter or the shul's site.
event_shul.unsure: Leave it blank; the typical band beside the box is a starting point.

event_seats.q: What do the High Holiday seats cost on top of dues?
event_seats.what: Type zero if seats come with membership.

event_sukkot.q: What does Sukkot cost, a year?
event_sukkot.what: A lulav and etrog set for each who wants one, schach when it needs replacing, and the sukkah's own upkeep. A new sukkah is a one-time cost; spread it over its life.
event_sukkot.unsure: A hundred and fifty covers one set and the small things.

event_yomtov.q: What do the Tishrei meals and guests add?
event_yomtov.what: Nine yom tov meals across Rosh Hashanah, Sukkot, Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah, over and above the usual Shabbat table.
event_yomtov.unsure: A hundred a meal is a plain figure for a family with guests.

event_chanukah.what: Candles and oil, gifts, latkes, the party.
event_chanukah.unsure: Leave it blank if you do not do gifts; otherwise fifty a child is a common floor.

event_purim.what: Mishloach manot, matanot l'evyonim, the seudah, the costumes. The matanot l'evyonim part is tzedakah; list it on the tzedakah page too if you count it there.

event_pesach.q: What does Pesach add over an ordinary month?
event_pesach.what: The extra for kosher for Pesach food, matzah, wine, and what the kitchen needs. If the family goes to a hotel program, put the program's cost here instead.
event_pesach.where: Last year's April grocery bills against March.
event_pesach.unsure: The band beside the box is for a family at home.

event_shavuot.what: Two days of meals, cheesecake included.

event_mikvah.q: What does the mikvah cost, a year?
event_mikvah.what: A membership, or the fees per visit added up. Type zero if it does not apply.
event_mikvah.unsure: Zero if it does not apply; otherwise the band.

event_eruv.q: What are the small community asks, a year?
event_eruv.what: The eruv, the vaad hakashrut, the chevra kadisha, the community's own funds.
event_eruv.unsure: A hundred and fifty is a common total.

event_israel.q: Is there a family trip to Israel this year?
event_israel.what: Flights, lodging, the two weeks. Leave it blank if there is none.

shabbat.q: What does Shabbat add each week over weekday eating?
shabbat.what: Challah, wine, meat or chicken, dessert, the guests. Kosher meat runs at one and a half to two times the ordinary price, so this is the largest quiet line in the year.
shabbat.where: A Thursday and Friday shopping receipt, less what a weekday shop costs.
shabbat.unsure: The band beside the box; a family that hosts every week is at the high end.

campSleepaway.q: What does sleepaway camp cost, for one child, for the summer?
campSleepaway.what: The full session fee, canteen and the trip there. Scholarships and the sibling discount come off first.
campSleepaway.where: The camp's fee schedule; the deposit is usually due in winter.

campDay.q: What does day camp cost, for one child, for the summer?
campDay.what: The full summer. Often eligible for the dependent care account.

rateId.q: Which share of income do you give?
rateId.what: A tenth is the common practice; a fifth the generous measure. Choose Your own share to type something else.
rateId.unsure: A tenth. The page shows what it comes to.

customRate.what: Used only when the share above is Your own share.
customRate.unsure: Leave it blank and choose a tenth or a fifth above.

baseId.q: A share of gross income, or of income after tax?
baseId.what: Gross is the stricter reading; after tax is the widely followed one, on the view that the tax never reached your hands. The page shows the arithmetic under the one you pick; your rav decides.
baseId.unsure: Ask your rav. Meanwhile the page shows the figure under either.

taxAnnual.q: How much income tax for the year, all of it?
taxAnnual.what: Federal, state and city income tax, plus the payroll taxes, added up. Used only for the after-tax base.
taxAnnual.where: Last year's return, or the year-to-date tax lines on the pay stub scaled to twelve months.
taxAnnual.unsure: Take a third of gross as a rough figure for a two-earner family in the New York area, and refine it from the return.

barmitzvah.q: What will a bar mitzvah cost your family?
barmitzvah.what: Tefillin and the lessons, the kiddush, the seudah or the party, the trip if there is one. Applied to every boy.
barmitzvah.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed. A kiddush and a meal at home sits at the low end.

batmitzvah.q: What will a bat mitzvah cost your family?
batmitzvah.what: The celebration, the chesed project, the trip if there is one. Applied to every girl.
batmitzvah.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed.

wedding.q: What will a wedding cost, the whole of it?
wedding.what: Both sides together. The share below says how much of it is yours.
wedding.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed.

weddingShare.q: Which convention does your family follow?
weddingShare.what: FLOP has the chatan's side pay flowers, liquor, orchestra and photography, roughly a third; the kallah's side the rest. Split down the middle is common now. Choose Your own share to type it.

customShare.q: Your share of a wedding, as a percent?
customShare.what: Used only when the convention above is Your own share.
customShare.unsure: Leave it blank and pick a convention above.

weddingAge.q: At what age do you expect the children to marry?
weddingAge.what: Places each wedding in a year. Modern Orthodox weddings cluster in the early and mid twenties.

support.q: What will you give a young couple in a year?
support.what: Help while they are in graduate school, yeshiva or the first job. Rent, tuition, a car. Type what you expect to give, not what you would like to.
support.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed; type zero if you do not plan to.

supportYears.q: For how many years after the wedding?
supportYears.what: Each year is a stop on the line for each child.

simchaMonthly.q: What goes aside for simchas now, each month?
simchaMonthly.what: The picture page counts this as the actual line. The simchas page compares it with the set-aside that would meet every simcha on time.
simchaMonthly.unsure: Type zero if nothing is set aside yet.

aliyahOn.what: Yes adds the pilot trip, the lift and the first months to the line, in the year you name.

aliyahYear.what: The year the family means to land.
aliyahYear.unsure: Next year is assumed until you type one.

aliyah_pilot.q: What will the pilot trip cost?
aliyah_pilot.what: The trip to choose a community, a school and a street.
aliyah_pilot.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed.

aliyah_lift.what: Shipping a container of the household's things. Nefesh B'Nefesh's calculator gives a current quote.
aliyah_lift.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed.

aliyah_landing.q: What will the first three months cost?
aliyah_landing.what: Rent and deposits, a car, appliances, ulpan, the school's absorption fees, before the stipend and the first Israeli paycheck.
aliyah_landing.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical band is used, marked assumed.

price.what: The house you are looking at, or the one you own if you want to see what it costs to carry today. Leave it blank to use the community's typical price.
price.unsure: Leave it blank and pick a community.

downShare.q: How much of the price goes down?
downShare.what: As a percent. Twenty avoids mortgage insurance; less is possible and costs more a month.

rate.what: The rate quoted, as a percent a year.
rate.where: The lender's quote, or this week's published average.
rate.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical rate is used.

years.what: Thirty is the usual term; fifteen costs more a month and far less in all.

taxRate.q: What is property tax as a share of the price, a year?
taxRate.what: Bergen County towns run above two and a half percent; New York City and Maryland near one. Leave it blank to use the community's typical rate.
taxRate.where: The listing's tax line divided by the price; the town's assessor site for the rate after a sale.
taxRate.unsure: Pick a community and leave it blank.

insuranceRate.q: What is homeowner's insurance as a share of the price, a year?
insuranceRate.what: Around four tenths of a percent inland; more near the coast.
insuranceRate.unsure: Leave it blank and the typical rate is used.

currentHousing.q: What does the home cost now, a month?
currentHousing.what: Rent, or the mortgage payment with tax and insurance. The picture page uses this as the housing line; the home page shows the difference against the house you are pricing.
currentHousing.unsure: The rent, or the mortgage statement's total payment.

emergency.q: How much is in the emergency fund today?
emergency.what: Cash you would use if a paycheck stopped: savings and checking above the month's bills. Not retirement, not the 529s.

leanMonth.q: What does a lean month cost?
leanMonth.what: The mortgage or rent, tuition's monthly share, food, utilities, insurance, the minimum on every debt, and nothing optional. The emergency fund is measured against it.
leanMonth.unsure: Take the picture page's lines a month plus the ordinary groceries and bills.

lifeCover.q: How much term life cover is in force, both parents added up?
lifeCover.what: The death benefit of every policy, including the group policy through work. The guide for a family with tuition ahead is twelve times income.
lifeCover.where: The policy declarations; the benefits portal for the group cover.
lifeCover.unsure: The group cover through work is usually one or two times salary; start there.

hasWill.q: Is there a will with a halachic clause?
hasWill.what: Torah inheritance rules and state law differ. A will that adds a shtar chatzi zachar or a rabbinically drafted clause lets both hold at once, and names guardians for the children.
hasWill.unsure: No, if you have not signed one with a lawyer.

hasDisability.q: Is there disability cover on the earners?
hasDisability.what: Long-term disability that replaces part of income if you cannot work. Group cover through work counts.
hasDisability.unsure: Check the benefits portal; most employers offer it.

retirementBalance.q: What is saved for retirement today, both of you?
retirementBalance.what: Every 401(k), 403(b), IRA and pension balance added up.
retirementBalance.where: The statements or the plan portals.
retirementBalance.unsure: Leave it blank; the picture page says what it needs.

returnRate.q: What growth to assume, a year?
returnRate.what: After inflation. Four to five percent is the sober figure for a balanced portfolio; seven assumes stocks alone and no bad decade.
